advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test that runs the gate/shellcheck at '-S error' over the VULNERABLE fixture and asserts it passes green (SC2115 NOT caught), pinning the second direction the docstring claims.
evidence: tests/unit/test_check_shellcheck.py:65: `assert chk.SEVERITY == "warning"`
Docstring claim tests/unit/test_check_shellcheck.py:8-10: 'The severity floor is therefore a behavioural contract ... a gate raised to -S error would run green over the exact line'
Commit message: 'Both directions are pinned by tests.'
ABSENCE: search for 'error' in the test file yields only comment/docstring lines (9, 56, 63); no test invokes run_shellcheck or main with severity 'error' over VULNERABLE to assert it passes green.

Named violating input: if SEVERITY were changed to 'error', VULNERABLE (`rm -rf "${dir}"/*`, SC2115 at warning) would pass the gate; only the constant-equality assertion would catch this, not any behavioral test of the gate output.
advisory.finding: The severity contract's second direction ('-S error runs GREEN over the SC2115 line') — the entire behavioral justification for pinning SEVERITY='warning' — is asserted only via the constant-equality check `chk.SEVERITY == 'warning'`, never by driving shellcheck at '-S error' over the VULNERABLE fixture. The commit and docstrings claim 'Both directions are pinned by tests', but only the warning direction is behaviorally exercised.
scenarios: A future refactor computes severity dynamically or reads it from config: the constant-equality test still passes/adapts, but no test proves SC2115 is actually caught at that severity and missed at 'error'.
The two-direction claim gives false confidence that regressing the threshold is behaviorally guarded.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: `code, output = chk.run_shellcheck(repo, [Path('purge.sh')], shutil.which('shellcheck'))` invoked with severity 'error' (parametrize run_shellcheck or call shellcheck directly with '-S error') and assert `code == 0` / `'SC2115' not in output`, demonstrating that raising the floor re-opens the hole.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a discover() test that creates a symlinked *.sh and asserts it is excluded from the returned list.
evidence: scripts/check_shellcheck.py:69: `if not path.is_file() or path.is_symlink():`
ABSENCE: search for 'symlink' in tests/unit/test_check_shellcheck.py returns no matches; test_discover_skips_vendored_and_scratch_directories covers EXCLUDED_DIRS only.
Named violating input: a symlink `link.sh -> real.sh` in the repo root — the `path.is_symlink()` guard is meant to skip it, but no test exercises this added branch.
advisory.finding: The symlink-exclusion branch in discover() (`or path.is_symlink()`) is newly added code with no test asserting a symlinked *.sh is excluded from discovery.
scenarios: A regression that drops the is_symlink() check (e.g. simplifying discover) would go undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have check_shellcheck.py discover scripts from the git-tracked set (e.g. `git ls-files '*.sh'`) so the gate matches AC-1 and does not drift on untracked working-tree files.
evidence: scripts/check_shellcheck.py:65: `for path in root.rglob("*.sh"):`
scripts/check_shellcheck.py:44-53: EXCLUDED_DIRS is a hardcoded set (.venv,.git,.claude,.tickets-tracker,.tickets-hotpath-authoritative,node_modules) — anything else untracked is still linted
Ticket AC-1: 'make lint runs ShellCheck at -S warning over every tracked *.sh file' — the implementation walks the filesystem, not `git ls-files`, so tracked vs present diverge.
advisory.finding: discover() enumerates *.sh via filesystem rglob over the working tree (minus a fixed EXCLUDED_DIRS set) rather than the git-tracked file set, diverging from the ticket's AC-1 ('every tracked *.sh') — untracked/local scratch scripts in a contributor's tree are linted, and the committed-tree cleanliness test can pass in CI while failing locally (or vice-versa) purely from untracked files, i.e. gate drift.
scenarios: A contributor has an untracked local `experiment.sh` with a warning-level finding; `make lint` fails on their machine but the same finding never appears in CI (the file isn't committed), producing confusing non-reproducible gate behaviour.
A new gitignored tooling dir outside EXCLUDED_DIRS ships vendored shell; the gate lints it and fails on code the repo does not own.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the resolved shellcheck reports the pinned version (`version: 0.11.0`) before trusting the gate, mirroring test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py.
evidence: scripts/check_shellcheck.py:96: `binary = shutil.which("shellcheck")`
tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py:146: `assert "version: 0.11.0" in version`
Docstring lines 19-24 assert shellcheck 'comes from shellcheck-py, pinned exactly' as the contract, but no version check enforces it in this gate.
dropped.finding: The gate accepts any `shellcheck` binary found on PATH and never verifies it is the exactly-pinned shellcheck-py 0.11.0. The module docstring and the sibling test (test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py asserts `version: 0.11.0`) treat the pinned version as load-bearing, but check_shellcheck.py only calls shutil.which('shellcheck'); a stale system-wide shellcheck with a different SC catalog or severity mapping would silently satisfy the gate.
scenarios: A contributor has an OS-package shellcheck earlier on PATH than the venv's shellcheck-py; the gate runs the wrong version and its severity/SC coverage may diverge from CI.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert discover() returned a non-empty file set (or otherwise prove the walk ran) for the default repo-root invocation before returning success.
evidence: scripts/check_shellcheck.py:77-78: `if not files:\n        return 0, ""`
scripts/check_shellcheck.py:101-114: main() runs discover() then run_shellcheck() and returns 0 on empty with no liveness/non-empty assertion.
Litmus: in the world 'discover walked the wrong root and found zero scripts' the gate emits the same PASS as 'walked the real tree, all clean'.
dropped.finding: When discover() returns no files, run_shellcheck returns (0, "") and main() returns 0 without any assertion that the tree walk actually produced files. A misconfigured or wrong --root (empty/incorrect directory) yields a green pass indistinguishable from 'checked and everything clean' — the gate reports success by producing nothing.
scenarios: --root passed a wrong path in CI/hook wiring; a future refactor moves scripts and discover silently matches none.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (and ideally test) that the ShellCheck gate cannot analyse `$${...}`-escaped regions of Terraform templatefile sources, or lint the rendered form, so user_data.sh's root-privileged post-render code is not silently unguarded.
evidence: infra/terraform/main.tf:63: `user_data = templatefile("${path.module}/user_data.sh", {`
infra/terraform/user_data.sh:113-115: `# shellcheck disable=SC2066` then `for name in "$${!PARAMS[@]}"; do` / `key="$${PARAMS[$name]}"`

Commit message claims the file 'stays gated for real future findings rather than excluded', but ShellCheck reads the `$$`-escaped regions as literals pre-render, so genuine hazards written in `$${...}` form (including SC2115-shape `rm -rf` on a `$${var}`) are invisible to the gate on exactly this root-privileged file.
dropped.finding: The ShellCheck gate lints infra/terraform/user_data.sh in its unrendered templatefile() form, so ShellCheck sees `$${...}` as literal `$$` and cannot analyse the post-render array-iteration/secret-writing code; the gate's SC2115/quoting protection therefore does NOT cover the escaped-brace regions of the repo's highest-blast-radius script (root cloud-init that writes SSM secrets to /etc/rebar/.env).
scenarios: A future edit adds an unguarded destructive command inside a `$${...}`-escaped region of user_data.sh; ShellCheck reads it pre-render as `$$...` and emits nothing, so the gate that exists specifically to catch SC2115 runs green over it.
An operator assumes user_data.sh has the same ShellCheck coverage as plain scripts and relies on the gate for the root cloud-init path.
